title: Tenant Priority Epochs and Soft-Burst Policy for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Maya Chen
background: Large tenants purchasing Dedicated pools need predictable latency and throughput while smaller tenants want economical usage of idle capacity. Current reserved pools are static and binary: either fully reserved or on best-effort. This leads to frequent cold starts, inefficient utilization, and complicated manual negotiations for short-term increases in capacity.
problem_statement: We need a tenant-facing policy that provides time-bounded, priority-based reservations (epochs) and a controlled soft-burst mechanism that lets lower-priority tenants safely consume unused capacity without compromising guaranteed SLAs for higher-priority tenants.
goals: Introduce 'priority epochs' — short, schedulable reservations (e.g., 5m–6h) a tenant can request and receive with clear guarantees
Implement soft-burst borrowing: allow tenants to use spare capacity with preemptible slots and graceful degradation paths
Ensure higher-priority tenants experience no SLA regression when soft-bursting occurs
Provide observability and billing signals to show cost/latency impact of epochs and bursts
Create a safe rollout path with feature flags, canary tenants, and abort/on-call playbooks
non_goals: Replace long-term committed reserved contracts (monthly/annual) — this augments short-term operational needs
Building a marketplace or auction-based real-time pricing engine in this phase
Major runtime/kernel-level execution optimizations — rely on existing batching/eviction primitives
success_metrics: Epoch reservation success rate >= 98% (requests that start with the promised min slots within the epoch window)
No more than 0.5% increase in P99 latency for tenants with active guaranteed reservations after soft-burst activation
Soft-burst utilization increases overall Dedicated pool utilization by at least 12% in pilot clusters
Customer satisfaction (NPS/CSAT) for tenants using epochs >= baseline after 3 months
Operational incidents attributable to burst preemption <= 1 per month in pilot phase
user_stories: As an infra admin for Tenant A, I want to schedule a 30-minute high-priority epoch for a product launch so that my requests get guaranteed slots during that window
As a small-tenant developer, I want to enable 'soft-burst' on my account so my low-priority jobs can opportunistically use idle Dedicated capacity and reduce my costs
As an SRE, I want automatic preemption logs and eviction reasons so I can troubleshoot regressions when tenants are preempted
As a billing analyst, I want per-epoch charge lines and burst usage summary so I can reconcile customer invoices
requirements: API: Create/Cancel/List priority epochs with start_time, duration, min_capacity, max_capacity, priority_level
Policy: Scheduler honors epochs in order of priority_level then epoch creation time; epochs map to 'guaranteed slots' that cannot be consumed by soft-burst borrowers
Soft-burst policy: Borrowers receive preemptible slots labeled with eviction_score computed from tenant_priority, time_in_slot, and cost_weight

Fallback: Preempted soft-burst requests must be able to immediately fall back to a configurable policy: retry (with backoff), switch to a lower-cost model variant, or return a graceful degradation response
Observability: Console and metrics export showing epoch allocations, soft-burst occupancy, preemption events, and per-tenant latency/cost deltas
Billing: Create chargeable usage logs per-epoch and per-burst-minute for downstream invoicing
Controls: Admin toggle to disable soft-burst globally and per-pool; per-tenant opt-in flag
SLO safety: System should guarantee that tenants with active epochs see <1% eviction from their reserved slots except during explicit maintenance windows
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/dedicated/epochs returns 201 and a reservation ID when requested min_capacity is satisfiable in pilot pool
Scheduler: When an epoch is active, resources equal to min_capacity are not allocated to any soft-burst consumer for the epoch duration
Preemption: A simulated soft-burst consumer is evicted within 500ms of a higher-priority epoch needing the slot; eviction reason is logged and exposed in metrics
Fallback behavior: In test harness, preempted requests follow the configured fallback (retry or model downgrade) and do not return 500s more than baseline retry failure rate
Telemetry: Console shows epoch timelines and a dashboard chart with a soft-burst occupancy metric incrementing during pilot runs
Billing: Usage export includes epoch_id and per-minute burst consumption rows and ties to tenant billing account
Canary rollout: Feature toggled on in 2 internal pilot accounts, no P99 latency regressions, then expanded to 10 pilot customers with monitoring alerts enabled
tech_considerations: Use existing reservation bookkeeping in control plane; extend to support ephemeral epochs with TTL
Eviction scoring should be composable with existing fairshare logic — implement a 'burst_priority' additive factor
KV cache and batching impact: reserved epochs should retain cold-start prevention knobs (warm pools) to avoid latency cliffs
State cleanup: epochs must auto-expire and force-evict soft-burst holders; ensure no dangling allocations after crash/restart
DB schemas: append epoch_id to allocation records and billing exports; consider GSI for querying active epochs
Rate limits: API rate-limit epoch creation to prevent abuse (e.g., 10 epoch requests/min per tenant)
Security: epoch create/cancel must respect RBAC — only tenant admins or service accounts can schedule guaranteed epochs
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (development): Implement API + scheduler hooks, unit/integration tests against the simulator
Phase 1 (internal canary): Enable feature for 2 Redwood-internal Dedicated tenants and validate metrics for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (customer pilot): Opt-in pilot with 10 customers, observe utilization and incident rate for 4 weeks
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): Expand to 50+ tenants behind feature flag with automated rollback triggers tied to latency/cost thresholds
Phase 4 (GA): Expose self-serve epoch scheduling in Console, add billing exports and docs
open_questions: Should epochs support fractional GPU/share guarantees or integer slot counts only?
What is the optimal default for min_capacity and max_capacity bounds for 1–24h epochs?
Do we bill soft-burst minutes at standard rate or discounted/economy rate to incentivize usage?
How should we expose epoch conflict resolution in Console (automatic suggestions vs manual negotiation)?
